top_strength: The clock explanation was clean and complete — he covered start-on-arrival, the 2.5 hour minimum, and 15-minute prorated increments in one clear pass, and he tied prep work directly to a lower bill ('anything you do before the movers arrive would save you money').
coaching_note: He lost a ready-to-book customer at the finish line. She asked 'how do I get this process started, how do I do it online?' — a buying signal — and he answered with a soft 'if you've got a few more minutes' instead of an actual next step. There was no confirmation email, no link, no hours, no direct number, so she left with nothing to act on and had to promise a callback. Non-negotiable close sequence on every call: offer to lock the date, state no deposit and no reschedule fee, then say 'I'm sending you a confirmation email right now with the bolded details — reply if anything's off,' and give hours plus how to reach you. Second priority: he gave away $220/hr with no value stack behind it — No Worries $2,000 coverage, Meet Your Mover, and the On-Time Guarantee all went unsaid, which is exactly why she pushed twice for a discount on the truck.
phone_presence_notes: Zero name use, no affirmations or empathy markers, and he stacked four questions into a single turn while she was still answering the first — the customer stayed polite but the exchange read as a checklist, not a conversation.
